headline: Five Tickets, Fifteen Dollars, And A Season Still Underwater
paragraphs: Six games got graded, two were left alone, four produced action, and the model put out exactly five tickets at ten dollars apiece. Three won, one lost, one pushed, and the whole operation cleared 15.59 on fifty dollars staked. That is a 31.2 percent ROI on a sample so small you could lose it in a couch cushion. Still counts. We are taking it.

Western Michigan 42, Akron 14 made the best ticket look easy, with Western Michigan minus 15.5 cashing for 9.09 off a 3.7 point edge. The ugly one was Sacramento State plus 18.5 at Central Michigan, a 3.4 point edge and a 60 percent confidence that ended 28 to 7 the wrong way. Minus ten dollars and a reminder that the model's certainty is a mood, not a forecast. Buffalo covered and won outright, which paid twice.

Season to date: 190-244-13 across 447 plays, 4,470 staked, down 570.45, an ROI of minus 12.8 percent across eight real graded weeks. The model expected to hit 60.5 percent and has hit 43.8, a gap large enough to park the entire MAC in. There is a hindsight week sitting off to the side at 40-25-1 and plus 110.47, graded after the games finished, which is to say it is worth nothing and we mention it only to be transparent about ignoring it.
